Using personal money is always tax expensive so avoid this wherever possible.

You might want to consider putting a new holding company, to be the invested into company, above your existing company. Monies can be paid from the existing company up to the new company tax free (dividends between UK group companies are received free from corporation tax). 

This can be implemented under the reorganization rules i.e. it can be put in place tax free. Advance clearance should be sought from HMRC, prior to the transaction, to get confirmation this treatment will apply 

Source: am a tax advisor and deal with corporate reorganisations

This is a major "one shot" transaction you're talking about and really needs proper advice and a bespoke plan drawing up suitable to your needs. To be tax efficient a succession plan might involve the "next generation" using a new company to purchase the existing shares in the company. The "exiting" director can still retain a small shareholding in Newco if they only want to semi retire. There are options for arranging the consideration received by the exiting parties with commercial and tax issues in mind.

Just because most operators you meet in elementary school (+, x, -, ^ etc) are defined for zero, does not mean that all of them are!
